body: Its strange. Flash message should remove only when you access it. This should work by design.

Each time `Session` is started, it will increment the counter of each flash message by 1 (the counter starts at 0). If a counter is more than 1 the message will be removed. This is by design.

For your case, why do you redirect to home instead of login?
@qiangxue Its strange. Why not remove flash message after it requested?
Yes, this is supported too (see the `$delete` parameter in `getFlash()`). The current design is based on the feedback we received from 1.1.

> For your case, why do you redirect to home instead of login?

@qiangxue 

This is just an example (`goHome()` left from app-advanced SiteController).

There can be other usecases when user is redirected several times until final view will be rendered - and he will be not able to read flash messages.

repository.name: yii2

issue.body:
Enable to set custom number of requests after which flashes will be deleted automatically (see #3956) - so it could be set in components config if nesessary:

```
    'components' => [
        ...
        'session' => [
            'flashesQueueDepth' => 3
        ]
```

@qiangxue I've checked the code and starting to think that it may be better to make it totally straightforward i.e. message is there till its requested.

I'm not sure. All other frameworks implement flash in this way. Therefore, we should be extra careful. My biggest concern is that in case a flash is not accessed somehow, it may appear later and confuse users.
How it may be not accessed? User closed the page in process of redirection? Won't it cause the same effect with current implementation?

For example, you store several flashes at the same time, but only access one of them in the new request. 

IMO, the issue reported here is not really a valid use case of flash. By definition, flash represents data persisted till the next request. If you want some data to persist across multiple requests, then use session directly.

Yeah. Another example:
1. Open page `X` that sets flash.
2. Close that tab.
3. Open another tab and browse website for 2 more hours not getting to page `X`.
4. Get back to page `X` that reads flash.
5. Got a flash displayed...

Overall I agree that it's better to either show flash immediately or just discard it. Imagine you've left it for 10 hours and then you're getting back to your moderator page and it says that "post was successfully deleted".
